title: Guided workflow and accessibility for non-expert users

queue.claim: Inter-operator landmark placement error on 3D facial images is about 0.5–1 mm for crisp points (canthi, cheilia, subnasale) and 2–4 mm or more for gonion, zygion and orbitale. Novices are about 1.3–2× worse on ambiguous points. These values set the default user-pin σ (crisp 0.8/1.2 mm, nose tip 2 mm, nasion vertical 3.5 mm).
queue.query: inter-operator variability manual annotation 3D facial landmarks mm stereophotogrammetry reproducibility endocanthion gonion

queue.claim: On 2D in-the-wild face images, human annotators disagree by roughly 3–6% of interocular distance over full 68-point sets. The COFW human performance figure is about 5.6% normalised error.
queue.query: COFW human performance normalized mean error 5.6 Burgos-Artizzu robust face landmark estimation under occlusion

queue.claim: Blender Python API facts: Operator.poll_message_set exists since 3.0; UILayout.progress exists since 4.0; built-in gpu shader names lost their 2D_/3D_ prefixes and bgl was removed in 4.0; POLYLINE shaders are needed for wide lines on Metal/Vulkan; the sculpt mask is stored as attribute '.sculpt_mask' in 4.x; WorkSpace.status_text_set accepts a draw function.

queue.claim: ISO/IEC 29794-5 (face image quality) is published, and BSI's OFIQ is its open-source reference implementation, with component measures for sharpness, exposure, pose, expression neutrality, eyes open, mouth closed, occlusion and inter-eye distance. The ICAO/ISO 19794-5 minimum eye distance is about 90 px, with 120 px recommended.
